title: "What does a Discus-2c geometry reconstructed from published data look like?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 90.0   # s for this render, granted by the user
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0     # s for any one solve
PROBE_POOL = 200.0        # s granted for the probe
PROBE_SPENT = 4.7      # s the probe actually used

import aerosandbox.tools.pretty_plots as p
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

span_proj = float(main_wing.span(type="y"))
area_proj = float(main_wing.area(type="xy"))
aspect_ratio = float(main_wing.aspect_ratio(type="geometric"))
mac_len = float(main_wing.mean_aerodynamic_chord())
fuselage_length = float(fuse.length())
htail_s = float(htail.area(type="xy"))
wing_dihedral_val = 3.0
m_empty = float(empty_mass_props.mass)
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{aspect_ratio:.2f}"`]{.hero-value}
[reconstructed wing aspect ratio]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** Reconstructed from published span ([`{python} f"{span_proj:.1f} m"`]{.key}), area ([`{python} f"{area_proj:.2f} m²"`]{.key}), and empty mass ([`{python} f"{m_empty:.0f} kg"`]{.key}), the aircraft matches the certified Discus-2c baseline. The airframe combines a multi-taper wing with forward root sweep, a [`{python} f"{fuselage_length:.2f} m"`]{.key} fuselage, and a T-tail (@fig-three-view).

::: {.callout-note}
## New assumptions
1. **fuselage length: `{python} f"{fuselage_length:.2f} m"`**, Discus-2c published length.
2. **horizontal tail area: `{python} f"{htail_s:.2f} m²"`**, Discus-2 T-tail sizing.
3. **wing dihedral: `{python} f"{wing_dihedral_val:.1f}°"`**, Discus-2 published dihedral.
:::
